title: Enterprise Synthetic SLA Validation Framework
author: Priya Raman
content:
Overview

This playbook defines a repeatable, instrumented framework for validating enterprise SLAs using synthetic traffic prior to and during customer cutover. It is intended for Customer Success (CS), Onboarding Engineers, and SREs to ensure predictable availability, latency, and inference economics for Dedicated and Private tenants.

Goals

- Give a single, opinionated validation sequence that maps synthetic test outcomes to go/no-go decisions.
- Provide concrete Prometheus queries, synthetic payloads, and run steps that can be executed by CS within 2 hours.
- Surface regressions that materially affect customer SLAs or cost-per-token before cutover.

Scope

- Applies to Dedicated and Private deployments and to hosted accounts with enterprise SLAs.
- Does NOT replace long-term load tests performed by Platform performance team; this is a deterministic functional+SLO check suite.

SLA and Synthetic Metric Definitions

Primary SLOs to validate (examples; match the customer's contract and tenant profile):

| SLO name | Target | Measurement window | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| P99 inference latency (inference.request.duration_seconds) | <= 700ms (hosted), <= 1200ms (dedicated) | 30m rolling | Measured at ingress e2e, including queue and KV cache access |
| Availability (http 2xx ratio) | >= 99.95% | 1h | Counts 2xx / total requests to model endpoint |
| Error budget burn (failed requests) | < 0.05% of tokens | 24h | Flag if synthetic increases failure rate |
| Median tokens-per-request cost delta | <= +15% vs baseline | 2h | Detects model fallback or quantization mismatch |

Test harness and tooling

- Recommended runner: synthetic-runner v1.3 (internal binary) or fallback: python harness + requests.
- Telemetry sources required: Prometheus metrics (ingress and runtime), Distributed traces (Zipkin/Jaeger), and token accounting from billing sidecar.
- Test user: create a shared service account for on-call that triggers synthetic tests and writes annotations to the tenant timeline.

Prometheus queries (examples)

- P99 e2e latency (last 30m):
  - histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket[30m])) by (le))
- Availability (last 1h):
  - (sum(rate(inference_requests_total{code=~"2.."}[1h])) / sum(rate(inference_requests_total[1h]))) * 100
- Error rate (last 30m):
  - sum(rate(inference_requests_total{code!~"2.."}[30m])) / sum(rate(inference_requests_total[30m]))
- Token cost delta (30m compare to baseline stored in metric token_cost_baseline):
  - (avg_over_time(token_cost_per_request[30m]) - token_cost_baseline) / token_cost_baseline * 100

Synthetic payload examples

- Representative customer short-turn prompt (JSON):
  {
    "messages": [{"role":"system","content":"You are a helpful assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the key points from this 150-word policy text."}],
    "max_tokens": 256
  }

- Long-turn conversational sequence (helps expose KV cache and attention scaling): run 10 turns with average 200 tokens per turn.

CLI run examples

1) Quick single-tenant check (curl):

curl -s -X POST https://ingress.redwood.example/v1/tenants/TENANT_ID/contexts/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $SYNTH_KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '@short_prompt.json' | jq .

2) Runner bulk test (using synthetic-runner):

synthetic-runner --tenant TENANT_ID --profile short-turn --concurrency 20 --duration 15m --annotations "pre-cutover:synthetic-sla-check"

Pre-cutover validation sequence (ordered steps)

1. Prepare tenant and telemetry
   - Confirm billing sidecar is enabled and token accounting metrics exist: token_cost_per_request, token_count_total.
   - Ensure Prometheus scrape targets include ingress and runtime pods for tenant.
   - Create run annotation in tenant timeline: "synthetic-sla-validation:YYYY-MM-DD".

2. Baseline collection (10m)
   - Run low-concurrency (c=3) short-turn profile for 10 minutes to collect a baseline.
   - Record baseline metrics and store them as a short-lived baseline with a tag (baseline_id).

3. Stress & stability pass (30m)
   - Ramp to target concurrency (based on customer profile, default 20) over 5 minutes. Maintain for 20 minutes.
   - Observe P50/P95/P99 and availability; annotate anomalies.
   - Run two long-turn sessions (10-turn dialogs) to exercise KV cache and memory growth paths.

4. Failure injection (optional, with SRE permission)
   - Brief 60s network egress loss to storage or slow KV lookup simulation. Validate graceful fallback and error rate thresholds.

5. Post-run analysis (15m)
   - Execute PromQL queries above to compute SLOs.
   - Produce a one-page test report (see Reporting below).

Go / No-Go criteria (example thresholds)

- FAIL if any of the following occur during the Stress pass:
  1. P99 > contract threshold for two consecutive 5-minute windows.
  2. Availability < 99.90% during the 30m stress window.
  3. Token cost delta > +25% compared to baseline.
  4. Unhandled errors (5xx or segfaults) seen in runtime logs more than 5 occurrences.

- WARN if:
  - P95 is within 15% of threshold or token cost delta is between +15% and +25%.

Runbook checklists (pre-cutover)

- CS Engineer: tenant config validated, timeline annotation created, customer notified of test window.
- SRE/Platform: Prometheus scrapes verified, alert suppression for synthetic run times configured.
- On-call: escalation contacts listed and reachable.

Failure modes and mitigation

- Symptom: P99 spikes with no corresponding increase in token count.
  - Likely cause: KV cache misses or increased queueing on runtime.
  - Mitigation: Roll back to smaller batch profile, enable prefix cache warm-up, open a high-priority ticket with Runtime team.

- Symptom: Token cost increases by >25% with similar latency profile.
  - Likely cause: Model switched to fallback variant or higher-precision quantization was selected.
  - Mitigation: Pin model variant to baseline, revert quantization change, and notify Model Onboarding team.

- Symptom: Availability drop to <99% during test.
  - Likely cause: Ingress throttling or misconfigured rate limiter.
  - Mitigation: Increase per-tenant rate limit temporarily, capture traces, and coordinate with Ingress infra.

Escalation path (concise)

1. CS Engineer -> On-call SRE (15m SLA)
2. On-call SRE -> Runtime Pager (30m SLA)
3. Runtime Pager -> Platform Eng & Model Onboarding (60m coordination)

Mapping to alerts

- Create ephemeral alerts active only for the run window:
  - SLO: p99_latency > threshold for 2 consecutive 5m -> pager to Runtime Pager.
  - Error rate > 0.5% -> page On-call SRE.
  - Token cost delta > +25% -> page CS Owner.

Reporting and QBR artifacts

- One-page test report (template below) to be attached to onboarding ticket and QBR:
  - Tenant ID, test window, profile used, concurrency patterns, baseline_id.
  - Key metrics: p50/p95/p99, availability, error rate, token cost delta.
  - Fail/Warn flags and root cause hypothesis.
  - Action items and owners with target dates.

Template (plain text):

---
Tenant: TENANT_ID
Window: 2028-01-08T10:00Z - 2028-01-08T11:00Z
Profile: short-turn + long-turn mix
Baseline ID: baseline-2028-01-08T09:40Z
Metrics:
  P50: 120ms  P95: 250ms  P99: 680ms
  Availability: 99.98%
  Error rate: 0.02%
  Token cost delta: +5%
Result: PASS
Action items:
  - Owner: Runtime Team -> Investigate transient GC spikes (ETA 48h)
  - Owner: CS -> Schedule follow-up synthetic after model pin deployment
---

Operational notes and best practices

- Always run synthetic checks outside of the customer SLA business hours unless explicitly agreed.
- Annotate every synthetic run; these become part of the tenant audit trail.
- Prefer representative prompts over random text — they catch semantic model fallbacks.
- Keep synthetic concurrency conservative on first pass; escalate to higher concurrency if stable.

Ownership and contacts

Appendix: quick troubleshooting commands

- Tail runtime logs for tenant: kubectl -n runtime logs -l tenant=TENANT_ID --since=30m | grep -i error
- Quick PromQL check for P99: curl -G 'https://prometheus.redwood.example/api/v1/query' --data-urlencode 'query=histogram_quantile(0.99,sum(rate(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket[30m])) by (le))' | jq .

End of document
